heading: INT. SALT-DRYING SHED - TIDAL FLAT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SALT-DRYING SHED - TIDAL FLAT - NIGHT
A long timber shed on stilts above the mudflats, open at the seaward end.
White pyramids of salt glimmer along the floor like small glaciers.
The tide is a sound out in the dark, patient and wet.
INES MARCHETTI, fifties, a brine-cracked woman in oilskins, stands at the foot of the largest heap with a lantern held low.
DORCAS WYNN, thirties, a county coroner's investigator in a clean grey raincoat that does not belong here, kneels beside a shovel that someone has driven upright into the salt.
TOBIAS LEACH, sixties, the shed's night watchman, sits on an overturned bucket in the doorway, his hands folded around a thermos.
Ines sets the lantern down.
Dorcas does not look at her.
Ines watches Dorcas's hands, and Dorcas watches the shovel.
You found it fast.
units.name: INES

units.text: It was the only thing standing.
units.name: DORCAS

units.text: Ines nods.
She steps closer.
She picks up a handful of salt and lets it run through her fingers back onto the pile.
She does it again.
She does not stop.
Tide turns at two. If you want the flat, you want it before.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: We want nothing, Tobias.
units.name: INES

units.text: Dorcas pulls the shovel loose.
The salt beneath is darker, damp, a seam of brown running down into the heap.
She sets the blade against it and pushes.
Who was working this stack last Thursday?
units.name: DORCAS

units.text: Nobody. It was closed.
units.name: INES

units.text: Somebody locked it. Somebody had the key.
units.name: DORCAS

units.text: Ines hands Dorcas the lantern.
She holds it a moment longer than she needs to, and she does not let go.
Careful. It is slippery near the edge.
units.name: INES

units.text: Dorcas takes the lantern.
She notices that Ines has not asked what is under the salt.
She says nothing.
She digs.
The shovel strikes cloth.
A sleeve, grey like her own, stiff with brine.
Tobias stands.
The thermos drops, rolling across the boards.
I told you to leave the tide to do it.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: Be quiet.
units.name: INES

units.text: You said the tide would do it!
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: Ines turns on him.
Dorcas, still on her knees, sets down the lantern and the light throws all three shadows long against the wall.
Which of you wants to tell me whose coat this is?
units.name: DORCAS

units.text: Nobody answers.
Out on the flat, the water arrives.
